Header: Colletotrichum falcatum , Glomerella tucumanensis syn. Physalossora tucumanensis

Prevention: Practice 2 year crop rotation to break the rapid built up of the disease.
Seed setts should be disease-free and treated with fungicide.
Field sanitation and hygiene should be followed.
Avoid ratoon cropping of diseased crop.
Maintain balanced fertilizer applications and also maintain organic matter of the soil.
Monitoring: Inspect the field at 10 day intervals.
Look for red streaks with ash gray centers on the midrib of the leaves.
Observe withering of the 3rd & 4th leaves from the top and later, the whole crown withers and droops.
When the plants approach maturity (September/October onwards), withering of the leaves proceeds downwards with the progress of disease.
In severe cases fruiting bodies of the fungus develop on rind just above or below nodes.
Do not allow irrigation from infected to healthy field.
Disease spreads more in hot weather.
Direct Control: Treat seed materials through aerated steam treatment at 50°C for 1-3 hrs.
Treatment with hot water combined with 0.1% carbendazim for 30 mins at 52°C.
The spread of the red rot can be prevented during the growing season by timely rogueing and burning of the affected clumps with utilization of the green leaves for cattle fodder.
The disease perpetuates from year to year through soil and planting the diseased canes or through decaying leaves, and also through the diseased cane lying in the field.
Ratoon crop may also help greatly in multiplication and penetration of the fungus.
Restrictions: Do not drink, eat or smoke whilst spraying chemicals.
Wear protective clothing, i.e. gloves, boots, masks and goggles while handling and spraying pesticides.
Thiophanate methyl @ 0.2% concentration is effective to control sett- borne infection of red rot
